Preliminary notification was issued on 25.06.2007.
The award was passed on 24.04.2009 and L.A.O. has fixed compensation of Rs. 56,45,560/- per acre.
Not being satisfied with the amount awarded, the claimant had filed objections before the L.A.O.
In pursuance to the objection, the L.A.O. has sent the reference to this Court.

After receipt of the reference from the respondent No.1,
this court registered the case and issued notice to both the parties.
The claimant and respondents have appeared through their counsels and have contested the matter.
.4. The claimant has filed claim statement stating that the award notice does not specify whether the compensation determined by this Authority is apportioned or not.

That the market value of the land has been under valued and the market value is not less than Rs. 1,500/- per sq. feet; that the land acquired has virtually ceased to be agricultural land and therefore,

This Authority ought to have therefore applied the law laid down in ILR 2005 Kar.4320.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed in (2009) 15 SCC 769, wherein it has been held that:
 "one of the recognized methods for determination of  market value is with reference to the opinion of  experts.
The estimation of market value by such  statutorily constituted.
Expert committees, as expert  evidence
can therefore from the basis for determining  the market value in land acquisition cases, as a  relevant piece of evidence.
It will be however open to  either party to place evidence to dislodge the  presumption that may flow from such guideline  market value.
We, however, hasten to add that the  guidelines market value can be a relevant piece of  evidence only if they are assessed by statutorily  appointed expert committees.
In accordance with the  prescribed assessment procedure (either streetwise or  roadwise or areawise or village wise) and finalized  after inviting objections and published in th e gazette.
Be that as it may.

guidance value has been fixed by the State Government after constituting expert's committee.
The respondent has not placed any evidence to dislodge the presumption.
Hence, the guidance value can be relied upon for fixing market value in the present case.
